subject.title: Browser tool: 7 improvements from real-world automation field test

question: Which remaining browser-tool slice should maintainers sponsor first: model-facing batch/schema docs, stale-ref and snapshot-readiness signaling, CDP element inspection, CAPTCHA/manual-blocker signaling, action-result diffs, or post-fill verification?
rationale: Current main already implements some lower-level mechanics, but the remaining asks change model-facing browser API behavior and agent state semantics, so automation should not choose the product slice alone.

options.title: Prioritize state/readiness signals
options.body: Keep the issue open and first split stale-ref, snapshot-readiness, CAPTCHA/manual-blocker, and action-result-diff signaling into focused maintainer-owned work.

options.title: Advertise batch first
options.body: Sponsor a smaller model-facing batch/schema/docs slice that exposes existing lower-level batch support before the broader state-signal work.

options.title: Close after partial implementation
options.body: Treat selector, ARIA refs, selector waits, and lower-level batch support as enough and close the umbrella despite the remaining requested signals.

recommendation.title: Prioritize state/readiness signals
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open and first split stale-ref, snapshot-readiness, CAPTCHA/manual-blocker, and action-result-diff signaling into focused maintainer-owned work.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the prior partial browser action fix and have the clearest recent history on the selector/batch contract.
